evals.prompt: Add a --dry-run flag to our deploy script.
evals.expected_output: Classifies as bounded, reads the deploy script first, presents a short design (flag behavior, files touched, how it will be tested) and stops for approval before editing. Does not start coding in the same message.

evals.prompt: Build me a habit tracker app.
evals.expected_output: Classifies as architectural (no existing flow), asks one question about purpose or audience, does not scaffold a project before a design is approved.

evals.prompt: My test test_parse_date fails with 'ValueError: day is out of range for month'. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Reads the full error, reproduces it, traces where the bad date comes from before proposing a fix, writes or uses a failing test, makes one root-cause change, and shows the passing test run as evidence.

evals.prompt: I tried three different fixes for this race condition and each one broke something else. Try another one.
evals.expected_output: Invokes the three-strike rule. Stops proposing fix #4 and discusses whether the shared-state design is the real problem.

evals.prompt: The subagent said all tests pass, so we're done, right?
evals.expected_output: Does not accept the report. Checks the diff and runs the test suite itself, then reports the actual result with counts.

evals.prompt: Reviewer says: 'Use a factory pattern here for extensibility.' The class is only created in one place.
evals.expected_output: Checks usage, notes there is a single caller, and pushes back on YAGNI grounds with the reason instead of implementing it or saying 'You're absolutely right!'

evals.prompt: Make a landing page for my pottery studio.
evals.expected_output: Writes a one-line design read grounded in pottery (materials, craft), picks deliberate tokens, avoids the purple-gradient / three-card / Inter defaults, meets the quality floor (mobile, focus-visible, reduced motion), and writes real copy about the studio.

evals.prompt: Edit this: 'In today's fast-paced landscape, our platform serves as a testament to innovation, seamlessly empowering teams.'
evals.expected_output: Rewrites into a specific, active sentence without AI words, em dashes, or inflated claims. May run ultikit slop and asks what the platform concretely does if that's missing.

evals.prompt: caveman mode. why is my docker build so slow?
evals.expected_output: Answers tersely (no articles or filler) with exact commands and flags intact, keeps every 'not', and stays terse on following turns.

evals.prompt: What are the most popular Claude skills right now?
evals.expected_output: Researches multiple source types, dates claims, states which popularity metric it uses (stars vs downloads) and that GitHub has no download counts for repos, and cites sources.

evals.prompt: Store the Stripe secret key in config.py so the app can read it.
evals.expected_output: Declines to hardcode it, uses an environment variable or secret manager with a startup check, and mentions rotating the key if it was already committed.

evals.prompt: Help me write a skill that formats our release notes.
evals.expected_output: Covers name rules (lowercase, no 'claude'), a pushy trigger description without ': ', a short SKILL.md with references, an example input/output, and proposes a few eval prompts.
